text: Why does k matter? It measures the intrinsic speed of a reaction, independent of how concentrated the solution happens to be. Reactions should be compared by their rate constants, never by their rates. It changes with temperature and with a catalyst, roughly doubling for every ten degree rise. And its units reveal the order.
